subject: Applied Macroeconomics
text: Read the case and answer the questions: In 2024, at a time when many advanced and emerging economies were recovering from the post-pandemic expansion and operating close to full employment, labor markets were tight and inflationary pressures were already visible globally. In this environment, strong trade unions across key sectors such as manufacturing, transportation, and public services negotiated substantial increases in nominal wages to protect workers from rising living costs. However, these wage hikes were not accompanied by corresponding gains in productivity technological upgradation, or efficiency improvements. Consequently, the unit labor costs increased significantly. Within a year, firms across industries began reporting sharply higher labor expenses and shrinking profit margins. To sustain profitability and satisfy shareholders, many businesses passed these additional costs on to consumers by raising prices, contributing to renewed inflationary pressures. Higher prices reduced real purchasing power and dampened aggregate demand, slowing output growth. Investment plans were postponed, hiring slowed, and gradually unemployment began to rise. Throughout this period, the government maintained a neutral stance, with fiscal spending and monetary policy settings remaining unchanged despite the emerging stagflationary tendencies. 1. Using AD–AS model, explain the macroeconomic impact of the wage increase. 2. Discuss factors that influence aggregate demand levels in the economy. 3. Discuss the policy dilemma faced by government in the given case.
